title: [Bug]: Application window does not have border shadow on KDE Plasma desktop environment (or not using mutter)

### Electron Version

21.3.2

### What operating system are you using?

Other Linux

### Operating System Version

openSUSE Tumbleweed 20221228

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Expected Behavior

Application window has border shadow on KDE Plasma Desktop

### Actual Behavior

No border shadow when using kwin. The border shadow is visible when using mutter on KDE Plasma Desktop.

_No response_

comments.author: participant3
comments.body:
> > Has to be a KDE issue. When I used GNOME in the past Electron apps had borders and window shadows like other GNOME apps. You can even control the border radius via plugins. So it's a KDE limitation. It's really annoying, I agree.
> 
> I reported this issue to kde devs, while they thought this was an electron issue.

KDE Plasma presents users with two primary options for window decorations: either utilizing the complete native window decorations stack or relying on the application's internal decoration. In contrast, GNOME offers a third option, where a border and shadows can be applied around a window irrespective of whether it has native or built-in decorations. This feature extends beyond Electron-based applications to include any displayed window, such as Steam. Steam is not an Electron app.

It's unclear why KDE developers are saying this is an Electron issue. There seems to be an expectation by them for Electron apps to implement their own non-native borders, simulating the appearance of native borders. However, this aligns more with theming, and any changes to native borders would not apply to Electron apps in this case since it would be fixed. As far as I know, window managers like KWin should have the capability to apply native borders around any window, which is what GNOME does with Mutter.

comments.author: participant18
comments.body:
Okay, to give some technical details. There is a Wayland protocol called [xdg-decoration-unstable-v1](https://wayland.app/protocols/xdg-decoration-unstable-v1). It controls whether an application window should draw the title bar and shadows itself or not. There is also older KDE-specific protocol called [kde-server-decoration](https://wayland.app/protocols/kde-server-decoration).

Now, what I'm seeing on Mattermost and Obsidian:

Mattermost 5.8 (Electron 29.3.0)
```
$ WAYLAND_DEBUG=1 ./mattermost-desktop-5.8.0-linux-x64/mattermost-desktop --enable-features=UseOzonePlatform --ozone-platform=wayland 2>&1 | grep -E '(set_mode|default_mode)'
[1277970.292] <email-scrubbed>_mode(2)
[1432605.895]  -> <email-scrubbed>_mode(2)
```

This means that the application requests server-side decorations.

Mattermost 5.9 (Electron 31.2.1)
```
$ WAYLAND_DEBUG=1 mattermost-desktop-5.9.0-linux-x64/mattermost-desktop --enable-features=UseOzonePlatform --ozone-platform=wayland 2>&1 | grep -E '(set_mode|default_mode)'
[1408129.110] <email-scrubbed>_mode(2)
[1412319.337]  -> <email-scrubbed>_mode(1)
```

This means that the application requests client-side decorations.

Same with Obsidian. However, it provides a setting to request SSD. In this case, KDE draws the decorations.

 So, the application requests CSD, KDE provides CSD. The behavior probably changed between Electron 29 and Electron 31 (or between MM 5.8 and 5.9).

P.S. This change probably comes from Chrome, not Electron itself.

comments.author: participant6
comments.body:
> It’s not obviously out of scope, that’s basically the reason why it worked before and does not work now. Where to go from here is obviously debatable.

Having server-side decorations (xdg-decorations protocol) means the compositor handles both the titlebar, and in the process the shadows, instead of the application, which is indeed out of scope for this bug as it is only about applications that don't opt into native titlebars but rather:
 
- Have Chromium titlebar buttons embedded into the window body (CSD with Chromium titlebuttons, e.g.: Visual Studio Code when titlebar is disabled)
- Use entirely custom titlebars (fullly custom CSD, e.g.: Cursor, iirc)

In both those CSD cases, not cases where a native titlebar is used instead when xdg-decorations is available, it is the application's job to render shadows around itself, thus what this bug is about (the lack of those very shadows it should be rendering).

> Also documentation still mentions the old behavior as the default one: https://<redacted-host>/docs/latest/tutorial/custom-title-bar

I'd personally report a bug to the documentation regarding that information being outdated.



This all being said, getting the client-side decoration Electron to render shadows and have appropriate 'window geometry' is the most likely missing thing here that is causing this issue in Wayland, I'd assume (the non-standard `frame-extents` that GNOME created in X11's case).

A workaround I've been using:

Alt + f3 » More Actions » Configure Special Application Settings » Add Property » No titlebar and frame: Foce = No
Before closing the popup copy the Window class (application) string

Then on System Settings » Window Decorations » Edit icon on selected decoration » Add Window specific overwrite » Matching window property: Window Class Name » Paste Window class into "Regular expression to match" (you can also use the button Detect Window Properties) » Hide window title bar: Always
